name: nest_home_control

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Bare uppercase one of: HEAT, COOL, OFF. HEATCOOL is NOT allowed. Variants like 'heat_cool' / 'heat-cool' reject.

inputs.name: target_temperature
inputs.description: Fahrenheit number (e.g. 72). Requires thermostat in HEAT or COOL — if currently OFF, pass mode in the same call.

inputs.name: fan_mode
inputs.description: Only 'on' works today (auto/off not wired through the bridge — they reject).

inputs.name: eco_enabled
inputs.description: true → MANUAL_ECO, false → OFF. Enabling requires HEAT or COOL; cannot enable from OFF (FAILED_PRECONDITION). Read state first if unsure.

inputs.name: get_status
inputs.description: true to explicitly read current state. Omitting all fields does the same.

arguments_prompt:
Read or change the Nest thermostat. Pass nothing (or get_status=true) to read current state.

Command execution order (when multiple fields set):
  mode → target_temperature → fan_mode → eco_enabled

Fields (all optional):
  - mode               — HEAT, COOL, or OFF. Uppercase. HEATCOOL NOT allowed.
  - target_temperature — Fahrenheit. Requires HEAT or COOL (pass `mode` in same call if currently OFF).
  - fan_mode           — Only 'on' works (auto/off reject).
  - eco_enabled        — bool. true requires HEAT/COOL (FAILED_PRECONDITION from OFF).
  - device_id          — usually omit (single thermostat).
  - get_status         — true to read state.

Examples:
  Cool to 75F (works from OFF too):       { "mode": "COOL", "target_temperature": 75 }
  Change setpoint (already in HEAT/COOL): { "target_temperature": 72 }
  Turn off:                                { "mode": "OFF" }
  Enable eco (must be HEAT/COOL):         { "eco_enabled": true }
  Read state:                              {}

When in doubt about current mode, read first ({}) then issue the change.
